heading: Making Broward More Affordable.
text: Caryl Shuham is running for Broward County Commission — to expand affordable housing, build flood resiliency, invest in public safety, and protect our environment.

heading: Elect Caryl Shuham for County Commissioner
text: Since 2018, Caryl Shuham has served the City of Hollywood as an elected City Commissioner. As Broward County Commissioner, she will continue her work to increase housing affordability through smart, resilient development throughout the County, with a special emphasis on underutilized commercial corridors. She will work to strengthen our local economy, protect the environment, increase public safety, preserve local history, and promote our unique neighborhoods.

heading: Elect Caryl Shuham for County Commissioner
text: Caryl holds a degree in civil engineering from the Johns Hopkins University and a law degree from the University of Maryland, and continues her private law practice as a construction lawyer — bringing real expertise in contracts, risk allocation, insurance, and bonding to county government.

heading: Elect Caryl Shuham for County Commissioner
text: Caryl and her husband, Marty, live in Hollywood with their dog Twyla. They are the proud parents of three sons — Simon, an aerospace mechanical engineer; Matt, a journalist; and Ben, a physician — all products of Broward County Public Schools. Caryl and Marty recently welcomed their first grandchild!

heading: Serving Broward County
text: From affordable housing and flood resiliency to public safety, the environment, and our local economy, Caryl has a record of delivering real results for our community.

heading: Expanding Affordable Housing
text: Caryl has worked to expand access to affordable housing — championing smart, resilient development that turns Hollywood's underutilized commercial corridors into homes working families can actually afford. She believes teachers, first responders, seniors, and young families should be able to live in the communities they serve, and she'll keep growing our housing supply on the County Commission.

heading: A Long-Term Plan to Stop Flooding
text: An engineer by training, Caryl has made reducing street flooding a priority. In 2025 the Hollywood Commission adopted a comprehensive Stormwater Master Plan — a long-term strategy to upgrade drainage, improve water quality, and protect our homes and property from flooding for decades to come.

heading: Standing Up to Reckless Development
text: Caryl has fought to keep oversized luxury development off Hollywood's barrier island — a hurricane evacuation route and environmentally sensitive land. She was one of just two commissioners to vote no on a beachfront mega-condo deal, rejecting “poor doors” that would segregate workforce renters and terms she called a bad deal for taxpayers. Broward should grow responsibly — not overbuild our coast.

heading: Protecting Our Environment
text: Caryl serves on the Broward County Climate Change Task Force and on the Board and Executive Committee of the Solid Waste & Recyclable Materials Processing Authority — and she is a consistent advocate for protecting our environmentally sensitive lands and natural areas, both in Hollywood and across Broward County.

heading: Investing in Public Safety
text: Caryl helped advance one of Hollywood's biggest public-safety investments in a generation — a new, state-of-the-art, hurricane-hardened police headquarters to replace a station in use since 1974, with a site plan approved unanimously by the Commission. The same voter-approved bond is equipping our police and firefighters with modern facilities, new fire apparatus, and updated technology — including body-worn cameras — to keep every neighborhood safe and accountable.

heading: A Stronger Local Economy
text: From the board that guides downtown redevelopment, Caryl has championed smart, sustainable growth along Hollywood's commercial corridors — including the State Road 7/US-441 corridor — turning underused properties into centers of business and jobs. On the County Commission, she'll keep fighting for better-paying jobs, more opportunity, and prosperity for all of District 6.
